ploidyspec report: dcCerAlpi1

Summary

Structure in this individual's assembly, read from the sections below; not inheritance and not origin. See docs/guide, Chapter 6.

Ploidy

2 haplotype copies of each of 36 chromosome numbers; the numbers form sets of 2 (no accepted pairs, but a balanced two-group partition), so x ≈ 18 and up to 4x relative to x.

Confidence: medium. Evidence: copies from the assembly (2 per number); no accepted pairs, but a balanced two-group partition (16 vs 20, z = 18.9)

Auto-like or allo-like?

Allo-like (disomic-like): the duplicated sets do not interchange, from a genome-wide partition (no accepted pairs). This is also what a long-rediploidized autopolyploid looks like.

Confidence: medium. Evidence: 32 chromosome numbers assessed: 32 split into lineages, 0 tetrasomic-like, 0 one divergent copy, 0 candidate

TE markers

Only the absolute marker fraction is available (two copies per number); it does not separate diploid, auto- and allopolyploid, so no reading is made from it.

Confidence: not assessable. Evidence: te_marker_fraction mean 0.1979

Rediploidization

Not assessable from this assembly.

Confidence: not assessable. Evidence: homeology map: 0% of the genome in 0 homeolog blocks, 0 chromosome pairs

Copy number and copy divergence (whole-chromosome matrix)

Hierarchically reordered, chromosome-number resolution

Same distance data as the heatmaps above, but collapsed to one value per chromosome NUMBER (haplotype copies aggregated away) and reordered by average-linkage clustering -- shows cross-chromosome (subgenome/ancestral-pair) structure cleanly, including diffuse structure with no individually FDR-significant pair. Red outlines mark individually FDR-accepted pairs from the homeolog test below. See INTERPRETATION.md's "checkerboard" section.
